head: 2ffbfae63f11a02ef045c477f7c2fa2880d8ac00
summary: Several added comments misstate the batching and duration APIs, including the public duration DSL and the non-finite duration hierarchy.  |  Several added comments omit or misstate exceptional and non-successful completion behavior, plus duration conversion edge cases.  |  Several added Scaladoc comments omit or misstate behavior that the implementations expose.

items.issue: The comment says reaching this context means `parentBlockContext` was null, but `AsyncBatch.parentBlockContext` is initialized and reset to this non-null sentinel. It is reached when no parent context has been installed, not when the field is null.
items.suggestion: Describe it as the sentinel used when no parent `BlockContext` has been installed; retain the always-throws behavior.

items.issue: The claimed maximum is not a maximum for a `SyncBatch` execution: `SyncBatch.run` repeatedly calls `runN(runLimit)` until the batch is empty. It only limits each chunk, whereas asynchronous batches are resubmitted after a chunk.
items.suggestion: Say it is the number of tasks processed per `runN` chunk, and distinguish the asynchronous resubmission behavior if documenting the starvation rationale.

items.issue: `Duration.Undefined` is also an instance of this abstract class (`val Undefined: Infinite`), but it is neither positive nor negative infinity. The class documentation therefore describes a false exhaustive set of its instances.
items.suggestion: Describe `Infinite` as the superclass for non-finite durations, explicitly including `Undefined`, or narrow the documentation to the inherited behavior of `Inf` and `MinusInf`.

items.issue: This trait backs the numeric duration DSL: its implementations construct `FiniteDuration` values from `Int`, `Long`, and `Double` receivers. It does not provide conversions from durations.
items.suggestion: Describe it as shared operations for numeric values that construct durations in selected units and optionally convert those constructed durations.

items.issue: All added generic overload comments claim that `C` is the singleton type of either `span` or `fromNow`. The signature permits any `C` with a `Classifier[C]`; `Classifier` is public and unconstrained. Moreover, the supplied marker value is not inspected by the conversion body—only the implicit classifier is used. This affects the `nanoseconds`/`nanos`/`nanosecond`/`nano`, microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, and day overload families.
items.suggestion: Document `C` as the type used to select an implicit `Classifier[C]`, without restricting it to the two built-in marker objects; state that the method invokes `ev.convert` on the constructed `FiniteDuration`.

items.issue: The new `@tparam C` description incorrectly requires a singleton marker-object type. The declaration accepts arbitrary type arguments, and clients can define `Classifier[C]` for non-singleton types.
items.suggestion: Change the tag to describe `C` simply as the type that selects the classifier/result type.

items.issue: The comment promises a pair for every `Duration`, but `d.length` and `d.unit` throw `IllegalArgumentException` for `Duration.Inf`, `Duration.MinusInf`, and `Duration.Undefined`.
items.suggestion: Restrict the stated result to finite durations and add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag for non-finite inputs.

items.issue: The documented `IllegalArgumentException` condition is incomplete: `Duration(d, unit)` also throws for a finite value whose nanosecond representation is out of range, before the match can determine whether it is finite.
items.suggestion: Document both cases: non-finite `d` produces a non-finite `Duration`, and finite values that cannot be represented also throw `IllegalArgumentException`.

items.issue: The comment documents only `NumberFormatException`, but validly parsed property values can cause `IllegalArgumentException`: a negative `maxExtraThreads` fails `DefaultThreadFactory`'s `require`, and non-positive derived parallelism can be rejected by `ForkJoinPool`.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag describing invalid numeric property values.

items.issue: The action is not run merely because this future completes: `thenRunAsync` runs it only after normal completion. An exceptional completion completes the returned future exceptionally without invoking `fn`.
items.suggestion: Say that the action runs when this future completes normally, and describe exceptional propagation.

items.issue: The comment says the action runs when both stages complete, but `runAfterBothAsync` runs it only when both complete normally; a failure prevents `fn` from running.
items.suggestion: Qualify the condition as normal completion of both stages and mention exceptional completion of the returned future otherwise.

items.issue: “Whichever ... completes first” is false for an exceptional first completion. `applyToEitherAsync` applies `fn` to a stage that completes normally; an early failure does not cause `fn` to run if the other stage later succeeds.
items.suggestion: Describe normal completion semantics rather than a simple first-completion race.

items.issue: The comment incorrectly says the action consumes whichever stage completes first. As with `applyToEitherAsync`, an exceptional completion does not invoke the action.
items.suggestion: State that the action is invoked for a normal completion and document exceptional propagation.

items.issue: The action does not run when either stage completes exceptionally; `runAfterEitherAsync` requires a normal completion.
items.suggestion: Say that the action runs after either stage completes normally, with exceptional completion propagated otherwise.

items.issue: The return description guarantees the same result as this future, but an exception thrown by `fn` can make the returned future fail instead.
items.suggestion: Add the callback-throwing case to the return description.

items.issue: The comment omits material exceptional outcomes delegated to `CompletableFuture.get`, including interruption and exceptional completion (and cancellation if this mutable `CompletableFuture` was cancelled).
items.suggestion: Add `@throws` tags for the delegated blocking-get exceptions, in addition to the blocking behavior.

items.issue: Only timeout is documented, but the delegated timed `CompletableFuture.get` can also throw for interruption, exceptional completion, and cancellation.
items.suggestion: Add the missing delegated exception cases alongside the existing `TimeoutException` tag.

items.issue: The summary implies `pf` is applied to every failure. In the transformation implementation, an undefined partial function leaves the original failure unchanged.
items.suggestion: Document that an undefined `pf` propagates the original failure; also cover a failure thrown while evaluating `pf`.

items.issue: The summary omits the material case where `pf` is undefined. The implementation preserves the original failure in that case rather than recovering it.
items.suggestion: State that an undefined partial function leaves the original failure unchanged, and document failures thrown by `pf`.

items.issue: `tryAwait0` uses interruptible shared-lock acquisition, so this method can throw `InterruptedException`, but the added Scaladoc omits it even though the adjacent `ready` documentation includes it.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws InterruptedException if the current thread is interrupted while waiting`.

items.issue: These comments present each member as a property value, but every implementation delegates to `propOrEmpty` and can return the empty-string sentinel when its system property is absent. This is especially material for optional properties such as `scala.home`.
items.suggestion: Document the empty-string fallback for each member, or replace the family with documentation that explicitly states the shared `propOrEmpty` behavior.

items.issue: The summary promises that the supplied fallback `Try` is returned, but the by-name fallback is evaluated inside a `NonFatal` catch and can instead yield a new `Failure`.
items.suggestion: Qualify the summary with the non-fatal-exception case, matching the `@return` text.

items.issue: The summary unconditionally says this returns a `Success`, although `Try(f(value))` returns a `Failure` when `f` throws a non-fatal exception.
items.suggestion: State that it returns a `Success` when `f` completes normally and a `Failure` for a non-fatal exception from `f`.

items.issue: The comment documents an exception only in prose; the project convention requires an `@throws` tag for thrown exceptions.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws Throwable always; throws the exception contained in this Failure`.

items.issue: It claims both finally bodies execute, but `{ body; other }` does not evaluate `other` if `body` throws.
items.suggestion: Document that `other` runs only after this body's normal completion, or change the implementation if both bodies must be guaranteed to run.

items.issue: The comment says it combines two `Catch` objects' logic, but the implementation delegates only to `or(other.pf)`: it discards `other.fin` and `other.rethrow` and retains this instance's values.
items.suggestion: Say that only `other`'s handler is used as the fallback, and explicitly document that this catch's finally and rethrow policy are retained.

items.issue: The comment describes the always-thrown exception only in prose rather than with the required Scaladoc exception tag.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws ReturnThrowable` tag stating that the method always throws this instance after storing `result`.

items.issue: The documentation omits the required two-or-more-element range condition. The delegated implementation expressly requires this; with fewer elements, its `start`, `step`, and `last` inputs cannot represent the sequence hash correctly.
items.suggestion: Document that this overload is only for ranges with at least two elements and that shorter ranges must use `seqHash`, as the delegated implementation specifies.
